graft.title: A baseline's check should fail on documents it hasn't recorded
graft.need: In vg-paradigms, `tend check --strict` passes (exit 0) while `tend doc record --check` lists eight files under licensing/ as unrecorded: committed to git at f46f07a but never signed into the log, so every project reads the baseline as having no licensing. Report unrecorded or changed-but-unrecorded documents under DOC_DIRS in `tend check` (an error under --strict, so CI catches it), or offer a git hook that records or refuses on commit, so recording is never a separate step to remember.
graft.use_case: The baseline's owner edits rules, conduct and licensing as files and commits them; autodyne's licensing switch was blocked by an unrecorded commit that CI let through.

answer.text: Done in tend 9facf9e. In a baseline repo, every document under its document folders that's added or edited since it was recorded is a contract error, so `tend baseline check` and `tend check --strict` (CI) fail until `tend doc record` runs there. In a project, `tend baseline check` warns (baseline.recorded) and lists them, and a command that needs one, like `tend baseline license`, says it's there but not recorded and where to record it, instead of 'has no licensing'. vg-paradigms' licensing and workflows are recorded now (its batch 01a109fe), so autodyne's switch is unblocked once that batch is committed there.
